lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Long ago, the earth was full of people — but their hearts had gone wrong.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Violence everywhere. Every thought twisted. Every day worse than the last.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the LORD looked at what he had made... and His heart broke.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But one man walked differently. His name was Noah.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Righteous. Blameless. A man who actually listened.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Noah. The end of all flesh has come before me. The earth is filled with violence because of them.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Make yourself an ark of cypress wood.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: An... ark. Here. In the middle of dry land. Where it has never rained like this.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No flood had ever come. No one would believe him. He had every reason to walk away.

choices.label: Trust the voice — pick up the axe 🪓
choices.note: "Noah did everything just as God commanded him." — Gen 6:22

choices.label: Ask for a sign first... 🌩️
choices.note: Noah waits. The silence is the sign. He picks up the axe anyway.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So Noah picked up his axe, and began.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Three hundred cubits long. Fifty wide. Thirty high. Cypress wood. Sealed with pitch.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: That is... enormous. Three stories. Rooms inside. A window at the top.

lines.speaker: wife
lines.text: Noah. The neighbours already think you've lost your mind. And now THIS?

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: I know how it looks. I'm building it anyway.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three hundred cubits is the length of three football fields. Built by hand, with no machinery.

choices.label: Follow the specs exactly 📐
choices.note: Every joint measured twice. Every plank cut to the cubit.

choices.label: Estimate a few measurements 🤷
choices.note: It'll look about right... but a joint or two will be weaker for it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Noah marked out the keel on the ground. The first timber went down.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Years passed. Ten. Twenty. The ribs of the ark rose above the treeline.

lines.speaker: crowd
lines.text: HAHAHA! Noah's still at it! Building his boat in the desert! Send for the doctor!

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: One plank. Then another. Don't look up. Keep going.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Fifty years. The ark's hull was sealed with pitch. The crowd's laughter got louder.

choices.label: Skip a coat of pitch to save time ⏩
choices.note: One thin section. The wood will probably hold... probably.

choices.label: Seal every plank twice 🔨
choices.note: Slow work. Honest work. Every seam watertight.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody believed him. But the ark kept growing, plank by plank, year after year.

lines.speaker: son
lines.text: Father... why keep going when no one understands what you're doing?

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Because I was told. And I said yes. That has to be enough.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Seven pairs of every clean animal. One pair of every unclean. Two of every bird.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And then something impossible happened. The animals came to Noah.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lions and lambs. Elephants and doves. Bears and deer. Marching, pair by pair.

lines.speaker: wife
lines.text: Are those... elephants? Walking TOWARD us?!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Noah provisioned the ark with food for every creature. It took days.

choices.label: Pack enough for a long journey 📦
choices.note: Every stall stocked. Every animal fed for weeks.

choices.label: Pack light — it won't last long 🤞
choices.note: Maybe the flood will be brief. Maybe not.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When the last pair walked up the ramp, the ark was full. Seven days remained.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the seventh day, the sky changed. The horizon turned the colour of a bruise.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The first drops fell. Then more. Then the sky opened.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Great springs burst from the deep. Floodgates of heaven broke open.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And then — from the outside — the LORD shut the door.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: That sound. The latch. From the outside.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No more choices. No more preparation. No more anything to do but endure.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For forty days, the rain hammered the hull without stopping.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The water rose until the highest mountains vanished beneath it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every living thing outside was gone. Only the ark floated on the face of the waters.

lines.speaker: wife
lines.text: Is it ever going to stop? The animals are restless. The children are frightened.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Keep feeding them. Keep the pens clean. One day at a time.

choices.label: Check on every animal yourself 🐘
choices.note: Exhausting. But every creature is calm and cared for.

choices.label: Let the family manage on their own 🙏
choices.note: They cope. But an unattended pen floods at the worst moment.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: After forty days, the rain stopped. But the water held its height for another hundred and ten days.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat. Still no land in sight.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: He opened the window and sent out the raven. It flew back and forth, never returning.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No news. No land. Just the raven, circling.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Seven days later: the dove. Please come back with something.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The dove came back with a fresh olive leaf in its beak.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Somewhere beneath the water — trees. Living trees. The earth was coming back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Seven more days. The dove went out — and did not come back. Dry land was waiting.

choices.label: Open the hatch and look 👀
choices.note: Blue sky. Mud. The outline of mountains. Real.

choices.label: Wait for God's word before moving 🙏
choices.note: Noah waits. It's the right call. The word comes.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Come out of the ark — you and your wife, your sons and their wives.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Bring out every kind of living creature — so they can multiply on the earth.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ramp came down. For the first time in over a year, Noah stepped onto solid ground.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The animals poured out — running, flying, leaping. The world filling back up with life.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The whole long year — the building, the waiting, the enduring — this was what it was for.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A year and seventeen days after the door was shut — Noah stood on dry land.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The first thing Noah did on dry land was not rebuild a house. It was build an altar.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He took one of every clean animal and offered it as a burnt offering.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Never again will I curse the ground because of humans. Never again will I destroy all life.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: I have set my rainbow in the clouds. It is the sign of the covenant between me and the earth.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Colour tore across the sky — red, gold, green, blue — a promise written in light.

lines.speaker: family
lines.text: All eight of them stood in the mud and stared at the sky. Nobody spoke.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The story looked like it was over. It was not over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Time passed. Noah planted a vineyard. He worked the soil. He waited for the harvest.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then he drank the wine. He drank too much. And he lay uncovered in his tent.

lines.speaker: son
lines.text: (Ham went out and told his brothers, mocking what he had seen.)

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But Shem and Japheth took a garment and walked in backwards, covering their father without looking.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The one righteous man, who built the ark and survived the flood, stumbled here.

choices.label: You are Shem or Japheth — cover without looking 🙈
choices.note: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem." — Gen 9:26. Dignity over exposure.

choices.label: You are Ham — go and tell 👁️
choices.note: "Cursed be Canaan." — Gen 9:25. The long shadow of a moment's disrespect.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The story doesn't end with the rainbow. It ends with a man who built everything right — and then failed in a tent.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And it ends with two sons who chose, quietly, to show him grace anyway.
